passage: "Jahnavi, can I ask something?" Rafiq said, walking beside her to school. "Sure." "Why do you always wear a dupatta? Does your family make you?" "Some days it's Amma's rule," Jahnavi said. "Some days it feels like me. Today it just matched my kurta." She grinned. "You're not the first to guess." "Sorry. I assumed." "Everyone does. My cousin wears hers for prayer, my friend Sana never wears one, and neither of us is wrong." "So you can't tell from looking." "Exactly. You'd have to ask, and listen." Rafiq laughed, embarrassed. "Okay. I'm listening. 😅"

qa.q: Who asked Jahnavi about the dupatta?
qa.a: Rafiq asked her, while they were walking to school.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling after Jahnavi answered?
qa.a: He felt a little embarrassed and sorry for assuming, as his apology and laugh show, and probably some curiosity too. 😅

qa.q: How could Rafiq ask about someone's clothing without assuming?
qa.a: He could ask an open, friendly question and really listen, accepting that the same item can be faith, family expectation, choice or style.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi feel when people guess about her dupatta?
qa.a: Somewhat tired of being assumed about, as 'Everyone does' hints, yet she stays friendly and explains patiently.

grounding: A teenager's dupatta can mean family rule, personal feeling or style, so others should ask rather than assume.

passage: After my thread ceremony I thought I'd feel different. Mostly I felt itchy. In the changing room before PE a boy asked if it was some fashion thing. Kalyani, who sits behind me in Bengali class, said, "My uncle wears one to pray, my cousin wears one because his mother insists, and I know a boy who just likes it." She looked at me. "Which are you?" I realised I had no clean answer. Ma wants me to keep it on. Dadu says it has to do with learning, and I like feeling close to him. Some days I tuck it under my shirt, some days I don't. I'm still working it out. - Arnab

qa.q: Where did the boy ask Arnab about the thread?
qa.a: He asked in the changing room before PE.

qa.q: What did Arnab feel when Kalyani asked which he was?
qa.a: He felt uncertain, since he had no clean answer; his reasons seem to mix his mother's wish, closeness to Dadu and his own feeling.

qa.q: How could Arnab reply when someone asks what his thread means?
qa.a: He could share what he knows or say he is still working it out, without needing a tidy answer.

qa.q: What does Kalyani's list of people show?
qa.a: It shows that the same thread can be prayer, family insistence or personal taste, so nobody should assume what it means for someone else.

grounding: A teen wears a sacred thread whose meaning mixes faith, family expectation and choice, and nobody can assume it.
